subject: Game Theory
title: Reserve Prices
description: Learn Reserve Prices in one minute.

hook.text: A reserve price is the minimum a seller will accept. Below it, the item doesn't sell.

buildup.text: Setting a reserve forces bidders to start higher, extracting more surplus from eager buyers.

discovery.text: The optimal reserve is above the seller's own value. Even risking no sale can maximize expected revenue.

twist.text: Set it too high and you scare away bidders. Too low and you give the item away cheaply.

climax.text: eBay data shows items with moderate reserves sell for more on average than those with none.

punchline.text: The right floor raises the ceiling.

quiz.question: What risk does a high reserve price create?
options: The item may not sell at all
